items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Benny was admired by a very successful negro bootlegger named George Ricks whom most of us knew very well

ctx.x: Benny was well known for organising musicians who had never worked together as a group and have them sounding as if they had been together for years. The arrangements he made were more difficult for the sax section than they were for the brass, but he had good men because he knew the ones he wanted and the brass section's work was very effective with the passages he wrote for the reeds.

Benny was admired by a very successful negro bootlegger named George Ricks whom most of us knew very well, and one of the reasons for Benny forming this orchestra was because George wanted to open a club and Benny to have the band there. The salary was not great but the other musicians, like myself, admired and loved Benny to the point where they would have worked with him for the pleasure of playing his arrangements, if a job actually could not pay.

George Ricks opened the ex-Connie's Inn and named it the Harlem Club. There was a floor show the same as Connie had but the entertainers were not big names although they were known in Harlem. The band was sounding greater every day and I was the main soloist in the trumpet section. Benny was beginning to play trumpet also but he had not brought it out until he had it under control.
